title: Compatible finite quotient-unit augmentations under completed pullback
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf{Q}_\ell$. For a morphism $h:U\to T$ of schemes and a cochain complex $P$ of modules over the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data], there exist chain maps $\gamma_n:h^*P\to T_n(P)$, where $h^*$ is ordinary completed-coefficient pullback and $T_n(P)$ is the $n$-th term of the finite pullback quotient tower [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. They satisfy $t_n\gamma_{n+1}=\gamma_n$ for the consecutive tower transition $t_n$. For every degree $i$, pro-etale test object $V\to T$ and section $x\in P^i(V)$, the map $\gamma_n^i$ takes the inverse-image unit generator of $x$ to the finite pullback unit generator of $1\otimes x$ [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined]. The index $n\in\mathbf N$ means quotient exponent $n+1$. No completeness, flatness, constructibility or immersion hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Modules on Sites, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules and section-tensor-product (Tag 03EK); Pro-etale Cohomology, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (Tag 099N(5)), quotient-unit construction before derived completion.

proof.text: The completed coefficient direct-image map commutes with each finite quotient projection. Forget commutative rings to rings. Its adjoint is exactly the chosen completed coefficient inverse-image isomorphism. Thus the ordinary module adjunction and the finite module adjunction form the coefficient square needed to transpose the quotient unit.

In degree i apply the general restriction/pullback mate to the quotient unit P^i -> Res_n(P_n^i). The mate unit formula says that on an inverse-image generator x it is the finite unit of 1 tensor x. Naturality of the quotient-unit chain map and the mate proves the differential equation, giving gamma_n.

Transpose the two proposed maps gamma_(n+1) followed by transition and gamma_n through the completed module adjunction. It suffices to compare sections on inverse-image unit generators. The finite pullback transition formula sends the first generator to the finite unit of the quotient transition of 1 tensor x. The quotient tensor transition sends this to rho(1) tensor x = 1 tensor x, the second generator. Extensionality proves the consecutive compatibility.

theorem frameworkQuotientAugmentation_exists {U T : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ T)
    (P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E T) ℤ) :
    ∃ γ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      ((proEtaleRingModulePullback h ((completed l E).ring T)
        ((completed l E).ring U) ((completed l E).pull h)).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj P ⟶ ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l E h).obj P).obj (op n),
      (∀ n : ℕ, γ (n + 1) ≫
        ((integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l E h).obj P).map
          (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op = γ n) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ) (V : T.ProEt) (x : (P.X i).val.obj (op V)),
        ((γ n).f i).val.app (op ((proEtaleBaseChange h).obj V))
          (((proEtaleRingModuleAdjunction h ((completed l E).ring T)
            ((completed l E).ring U) ((completed l E).pull h)).unit.app (P.X i)).val.app
              (op V) x) =
          integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E h n
            (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E T n).obj P).X i) V
            (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E T n (P.X i) (op V) 1 x))
